page.title: Handoffs
page.purpose: The scenario's primary surface. Work the queue of steps that no machine may take, and complete each one with everything else already filled in.

priorities.statement: Each row states what the human must do in one plain sentence — not what failed, and never a raw error.
The four terminal outcomes (completed, expired, cancelled, refused) must be distinguishable at a glance and never by colour alone.
Everything the agent already completed is visible before the human acts, so they can trust the checkpoint instead of redoing the work.
Completion is reachable by keyboard alone, start to finish.
priorities.notes: A handoff commonly arrives on a phone at an awkward moment; this is the normal case, not an edge case.

priorities.statement: The queue must be fully usable with no notification relay configured — the relay is an enhancement, never a prerequisite.

states.description: One or more open handoffs, newest first.
Nothing is blocked. Reads as a resolved state, not as a failure to load.
A single handoff is open, showing the wall, the required action, and the checkpoint.
The operator has confirmed completion and the resume is in flight.
Completed; the originating flow has been handed back its checkpoint.
The handoff passed its deadline. A terminal state with its own presentation — never rendered as a generic error.
Explicitly cancelled by an operator; terminal.
The viewer may propose but not act as this persona, so completion is unavailable and the reason is stated.
The handoff loads but the linked document binding cannot be resolved.
No connectivity; queued handoffs remain readable from cache and completion is disabled with a stated reason.
The queue is older than its refresh interval because the API or relay is unreachable. Labelled with its age so an operator never completes a handoff that has already expired elsewhere.
